## What the Numbers Mean

- **Against decoding first:** this is the case of a store that holds Steno bytes. It never has to decode a key to compare it, while a format without the order, such as SCSU or compressed text, must decode both values first.
- **Against UTF-8 bytes:** UTF-8 bytes keep the same order, and they compare with the same byte comparison; the difference is in the number of bytes, and UTF-8 is larger for most scripts (see [Encoded Size](encoded-size.md)).
- **Strings in memory** sort in the same order only with a code point comparison, not with ordinal comparison in the languages whose strings are UTF-16 (see [Matching the Order in Memory](../start/storing-values.md#matching-the-order-in-memory)).

[Working with Encoded Values](../start/encoded-values.md) shows how to compare, sort and search the bytes.
